title: Payroll Delay Length in Pocketwire Advance Late Fee Relief — Training Note
content:
On a Pocketwire Advance line, the payroll delay is counted in calendar days from the due date of the line's most recent advance to the date of the line's most recent autopay collection from a direct deposit. A payroll delay of at least 14 days adds 0.20 to the relief share; a payroll delay of at least 7 days but fewer than 14 days adds 0.10 to the relief share; a shorter payroll delay adds nothing to the relief share. The relief share is the fraction of the late fee that the payroll-delay relief returns.

## The ladder

| Payroll delay (calendar days) | Added to the relief share |
|---|---|
| 14 or more | 0.20 |
| 7 to 13 | 0.10 |
| Fewer than 7 | Nothing |

## Questions answered

**Which due date starts the count?** The due date of the line's most recent advance — the advance with the latest disbursement on the line's activity.

**Which collection ends it?** The line's most recent autopay collection from a direct deposit, that is, the latest repayment entry recorded as an autopay collection from a direct deposit. An autopay collection from the personal balance or a manual repayment is not this collection.

**How are the days counted?** In calendar days from the due date to the collection date, the due date itself being day 0.

**Where do the boundaries fall?**

| Payroll delay | Added |
|---|---|
| 14 days | 0.20 — at least 14 |
| 13 days | 0.10 — at least 7, fewer than 14 |
| 7 days | 0.10 — at least 7 |
| 6 days | Nothing — shorter than 7 |

## Worked count (hypothetical dates)

The line's most recent advance fell due on 3 June and the line's most recent autopay collection from a direct deposit is dated 19 June. The payroll delay is 16 calendar days, which is at least 14, so 0.20 is added to the relief share. Had the collection been dated 12 June, the delay would be 9 days and 0.10 would be added.
